title: Hamas releases the 20 remaining living hostages as Israel frees Palestinian prisoners
body:
On Monday 13 October 2025, Hamas released all 20 living hostages still held in Gaza, according to the Associated Press. All were men, and they were returned to Israel to reunite with their families. Israel began releasing Palestinian prisoners under the ceasefire deal. Reports cited some 1,900 or nearly 2,000 prisoners, and the AP said about 1,700 were Palestinians seized from Gaza during the war and held without charge.

The bodies of 28 dead hostages were also due to be returned. Israel's military said it was sending the remains of four to a forensic institute for identification and that Hamas still held 24. The Hostages Family Forum said only four of 28 had been recovered and called the delay a blatant violation of the agreement by Hamas.

US President Donald Trump met hostage relatives in Israel and addressed the Knesset, then co-chaired a summit in Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sissi. He said rebuilding Gaza might be the easiest part. Egypt planned to host a Gaza reconstruction conference in November, and the UN allocated an extra 11 million dollars from an emergency fund for Gaza ahead of winter. The Gaza Health Ministry said Israel's campaign had killed more than 67,800 Palestinians and does not distinguish civilians from combatants. The Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023 killed about 1,200 people in Israel and 251 were taken hostage.
